questions.text: Given that x + 3 is a factor of x³ + px² + 5x – 12, find the value of the constant p.
questions.markingGuide: Since x + 3 is a factor, f(−3) = 0. Substituting: (−3)³ + p(−3)² + 5(−3) – 12 = 0. −27 + 9p – 15 – 12 = 0. 9p – 54 = 0. 9p = 54. p = 6. Achieved: Correct solution for p.

questions.text: If z = mcis(nπ/5), where m and n are positive real constants, then find z¹⁵, giving your answer in polar form, in terms of m and n.
questions.markingGuide: Using De Moivre's theorem: z¹⁵ = m¹⁵ cis(15 × nπ/5) = m¹⁵ cis(3nπ). Also accept m¹⁵ cis(15nπ/5). Achieved: Correct solution.

questions.text:
Solve the following equation for x, in terms of k, where k is a positive real constant.

4 – √(kx) = ⁴√(kx + 4)
questions.markingGuide: Square both sides: (4 – √(kx))² = √(kx + 4). 16 – 8√(kx) + kx = √(kx + 4). Let u = √(kx). Then (4 – u)² = √(u² + 4). Squaring: 16 – 8u + u² = √(kx + 4). Alternatively: (4 – √(kx))´ = kx + 4. Expanding and solving: 8√(kx) = kx + 12, then squaring again: 64kx = k²x² + 24kx + 144. Simplifying with √(kx) = 3/2: kx = 9/4, x = 9/(4k). Achieved: Reaching line (1) — squaring correctly at some stage. Merit: Correct value for x.

questions.text:
The locus described by |z – i| = |z + 1| is a straight line.

Find the gradient of that line.
Justify your answer.
questions.markingGuide: Let z = x + yi. |z – i| = |z + 1| becomes |x + yi – i| = |x + yi + 1|, i.e. |x + (y – 1)i| = |(x + 1) + yi|. Squaring: x² + (y – 1)² = (x + 1)² + y². x² + y² – 2y + 1 = x² + 2x + 1 + y². −2y = 2x. y = –x. Gradient is −1. Accept a graphical method. Achieved: Reaching line (1) — correctly substituting z = x + yi and setting up the modulus equation. Merit: Correct gradient found.

questions.text:
Consider the complex numbers u = 2 + 3ki and v = 4 + 5ki, where k is a real constant.

Show that the complex number w = u/v will not lie on the line y = x in the Argand diagram, for any value of k.
questions.markingGuide: w = u/v = (2 + 3ki)/(4 + 5ki). Multiply by conjugate: w = (2 + 3ki)(4 – 5ki)/((4 + 5ki)(4 – 5ki)) = (8 – 10ki + 12ki – 15k²i²)/(16 + 25k²) = (8 + 15k² + 2ki)/(16 + 25k²). (1) So Re(w) = (8 + 15k²)/(16 + 25k²) and Im(w) = 2k/(16 + 25k²). If w lies on y = x then Re(w) = Im(w): (8 + 15k²)/(16 + 25k²) = 2k/(16 + 25k²). So 8 + 15k² = 2k, i.e. 15k² – 2k + 8 = 0. (2) Discriminant = 4 – 4(15)(8) = 4 – 480 = –476 < 0. As the discriminant is negative, there are no real solutions, so no values of k make w lie on y = x. E7: Correct conclusion with incomplete justification, OR complete solution with a minor error. E8: Correct conclusion with valid and clear justification.

questions.text: Write the complex number 1/(2k + i) in the form a + bi, where a, b, and k are real numbers, giving your answer in terms of k.
questions.markingGuide: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate: 1/(2k + i) = (2k – i)/((2k + i)(2k – i)) = (2k – i)/(4k² + 1) = 2k/(4k² + 1) – 1/(4k² + 1) i. Achieved: Correct solution.

questions.text: Find the value(s) of r so that the quadratic equation 2x² + (3 + 2r)x + 3 – 2r = 0 has equal roots.
questions.markingGuide: Equal roots when discriminant = 0: b² – 4ac = 0. (3 + 2r)² – 4(2)(3 – 2r) = 0. 9 + 12r + 4r² – 24 + 16r = 0. 4r² + 28r – 15 = 0. (2r – 1)(2r + 15) = 0. r = 1/2 or r = −15/2 = −7.5. Achieved: Correct solutions for both values of r.

questions.text:
One solution of the equation 2z³ + dz² + 140z – 200 = 0 is z = 6 – 2i.

If d is real, find the value of d and the other two solutions of the equation.
questions.expectedAnswer: d = −29, other solutions are z = 6 + 2i and z = 5/2
questions.markingGuide: If z = 6 – 2i is a solution with real coefficients, then z = 6 + 2i is also a solution. Using z = 6 + 2i: (z – (6 – 2i))(z – (6 + 2i)) = z² – 12z + 40. Then f(z) = 2(z² – 12z + 40)(z – a) for some real a. Expanding: 2z³ + dz² + 140z – 200. Comparing: 2(z² – 12z + 40)(z + B) where the constant term is 2 × 40 × B = –200, so B = −5/2. Wait: 2z³ + dz² + 140z – 200 = 2(z² – 12z + 40)(z + B). Constant: 2(40B) = –200, B = −5/2. z coefficient: 2(−12B + 40) = 140, −12(−5/2) + 40 = 30 + 40 = 70, 2(70) = 140. ✓. z² coefficient: d = 2(B – 12) = 2(−5/2 – 12) = 2(−29/2) = −29. So d = −29 and the third solution is z = 5/2. Achieved: Correct value of d, OR solutions for z found correctly. Merit: Correct value of d AND solutions for z₂ and z₃ found correctly with evidence of algebraic methods.

questions.text:
The locus of a complex number z is described by

|z – 1 – 7i| = 2|z – 4 – 4i|

The complex number a = 3 + ai lies on this locus.

Find the Cartesian equation of the locus of z, giving your answer in the form (x – a)² + (y – b)² = k and also find the complex number(s) a.
questions.markingGuide: Let z = x + yi. |x + yi – 1 – 7i| = 2|x + yi – 4 – 4i|. |(x – 1) + (y – 7)i| = 2|(x – 4) + (y – 4)i|. (1) Squaring: (x – 1)² + (y – 7)² = 4[(x – 4)² + (y – 4)²]. x² – 2x + 1 + y² – 14y + 49 = 4(x² – 8x + 16 + y² – 8y + 16). x² – 2x + 1 + y² – 14y + 49 = 4x² – 32x + 64 + 4y² – 32y + 64. 0 = 3x² – 30x + 3y² – 18y + 78. (2) x² – 10x + y² – 6y + 26 = 0. (x – 5)² + (y – 3)² = 25 + 9 – 26 = 8. Then for a = 3 + ai (where a is imaginary part), substitute x = 3: (3 – 5)² + (y – 3)² = 8. 4 + (y – 3)² = 8. (y – 3)² = 4. y = 5 or y = 1. So a = 3 + 5i or a = 3 + i. E7: Finding the two values of y but not connecting them to the values of a, OR complete solution with a minor error. E8: Correct solution, finding the equation of the locus in the required format AND both values of a.

questions.text: Write (√(2p) × √(√(5p) + √p)) / (√(2p) – √p) in the form a + √a, where p and a are real constants.
questions.markingGuide: Simplify: numerator = √(2p) × √(√(5p) + √p). Note √(2p)×√(√(5p)+√p) / (√(2p)–√p). Rationalise: multiply top and bottom by (√(2p)+√p). Numerator becomes 2p√(√(5p)+√p) + √p×√(2p)√(√(5p)+√p). Alternatively: = √(2p) × (√(5p) + √p)^(1/2) / (√(2p) – √p). Simplification gives 2p + √(5p²) / (2p – p) = (2p + p√5)/p = 2 + √5. Achieved: Correct solution.

questions.text:
In the Argand diagram below, the point (−2, 3) represents the complex number z.

Show clearly, in the diagram below, the point representing w = z².
questions.markingGuide: z = −2 + 3i. z² = (−2 + 3i)² = 4 – 12i + 9i² = 4 – 12i – 9 = −5 – 12i. Plot the point (−5, −12) on the Argand diagram. Achieved: −5 – 12i correctly plotted.

questions.text: Find the value(s) of the real constant d, given that z = 3 + di and z̄ = 10dz⁻¹.
questions.markingGuide: z = 3 + di, z̄ = 3 – di. z⁻¹ = 1/(3 + di) = (3 – di)/(9 + d²). Given z̄ = 10dz⁻¹: 3 – di = 10d(3 – di)/(9 + d²). (1) If 3 – di ≠ 0, divide both sides by (3 – di): 1 = 10d/(9 + d²). 9 + d² = 10d. d² – 10d + 9 = 0. (d – 1)(d – 9) = 0. d = 1 or d = 9. Achieved: Reaching line (1). Merit: Finding both values of d, with justification.

questions.text:
Solve the equation z⁴ + 81k⁴ = 0, where k is a real constant.
Give your solution(s) in polar form in terms of k.
questions.markingGuide: z⁴ = −81k⁴ = 81k⁴ cis(π). r⁴ = 81k⁴, so r = 3k (taking positive root since k is real). θ = (π + 2nπ)/4 for n = 0, 1, 2, 3. θ₀ = π/4, θ₁ = 3π/4, θ₂ = 5π/4 = −3π/4, θ₃ = 7π/4 = –π/4. So z₁ = 3k cis(π/4), z₂ = 3k cis(3π/4), z₃ = 3k cis(−3π/4), z₄ = 3k cis(–π/4). Accept equivalent forms. Achieved: One correct solution. Merit: Four correct solutions.

questions.text: Given that x + 1/x = p, where p is a real constant, then find the value of x³ + 1/x³, giving your answers in terms of p.
questions.markingGuide: Given x + 1/x = p. Square both sides: (x + 1/x)² = p². x² + 2 + 1/x² = p². So x² + 1/x² = p² – 2. (1) Cube the original: (x + 1/x)³ = p³. x³ + 3x + 3/x + 1/x³ = p³. x³ + 1/x³ + 3(x + 1/x) = p³. x³ + 1/x³ + 3p = p³. (2) Therefore x³ + 1/x³ = p³ – 3p. E7: Correct expression but without including clear communication. E8: Correct expression, including clear communication.
